notes.meaning: Believers are completely safe from God's final judgment because they belong to Christ Jesus. Being in Christ means a person is joined to Him by faith, sharing in His life. God may still lovingly correct and train His children, but He will never doom them along with the world.

differ.view: Believers remain free from condemnation only as long as they continually fight against sin and do not willingly yield to it.

notes.meaning: The Holy Spirit brings a new life-giving power through Christ that breaks the rule of sin and death. This new life is far stronger than the old sinful nature that once held people captive. Because of this spiritual rescue, believers are no longer trapped under sin's control.

God's law could tell people what was right, but human weakness prevented anyone from keeping it. God solved this by sending His own Son in a real human body that looked like ours, yet without any sin. By offering Jesus as a sacrifice on the cross, God broke sin's power and cancelled its hold over human life.

God did this so that the righteous standard demanded by the law could be fully satisfied in believers. Because Jesus obeyed completely in our place, His righteousness covers those who trust Him. True believers show this change by letting the Holy Spirit direct their daily lives instead of their sinful cravings.

differ.view: The righteousness of the law is actual holy living produced in a believer's daily thoughts, words, and actions by the Holy Spirit.

notes.meaning: People who follow their sinful human nature care only about pleasing themselves and chasing worldly goals. In contrast, those who follow the Holy Spirit set their thoughts and affections on what pleases God. What a person thinks about most shows who is truly directing their life.

Letting sinful desires run the mind leads straight to spiritual ruin and eternal death. But setting the mind on what the Holy Spirit wants produces deep life and peace. Following God's Spirit fills the soul with lasting comfort and quiet rest.

A mind focused on sinful desires is an enemy to God. It refuses to submit to God's commands and is completely unable to do so on its own. Human nature left to itself cannot fix its own rebellion against its Creator.

Those who are controlled by their sinful nature can never please God. Without faith and the Spirit's help, even a person's religious deeds cannot satisfy Him. To be accepted by God, a person must first receive a new spiritual life from Him.

True Christians are not ruled by their sinful nature because the Spirit of God lives inside them. If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ dwelling within, that person does not belong to Christ at all. The presence of the Holy Spirit is the sure mark of every real believer.

Even when Christ lives in a believer, the physical body must still die one day because sin brought death into the world. Yet the believer's inner spirit is full of life because God has declared them righteous. Physical death cannot undo the eternal life God has placed in the soul.

God raised Jesus from the dead by His mighty power, and that same Holy Spirit now lives inside believers. Because of this, God will also bring their mortal bodies to life at the future resurrection. The rising of Jesus guarantees that everyone who has His Spirit will one day live again in a glorified body.

Believers have a deep obligation to God, but they owe nothing to their old sinful desires. That selfish nature never did them any good, so they have no reason to follow its lead. Christians are called to live for the Lord who rescued them.

Anyone who continues to live for sinful cravings will end in eternal death. But if believers use the Holy Spirit's power to put sinful habits and attitudes to death, they will truly live. Defeating sin takes daily effort, but it can only be done with the Spirit's help.

All who are led and guided by God's Spirit are recognized as God's true children. The Spirit directs believers with patience and love toward what is holy. Following His quiet guidance shows that God has welcomed you into His family.

The Holy Spirit does not make Christians cower in fear like terrified slaves under a harsh master. Instead, God has adopted them into His family as His beloved sons and daughters. Because of this, believers can pray with childlike trust, calling God "Abba," which means dear Father.

The Holy Spirit joins with a believer's own conscience to give quiet assurance of belonging to God's family. He does this by producing genuine love, peace, and obedience in the heart. This inner witness brings steady comfort when doubts arise.

differ.view: The Holy Spirit gives an immediate, direct inward witness to the soul that precedes and is distinct from the testimony of a good conscience or holy fruit.

notes.meaning: Since believers are God's children, they are also His heirs who will inherit His kingdom alongside Jesus Christ. Sharing in Christ's glory also means being willing to share in His sufferings in this present world. Bearing trials for Jesus prepares believers to enjoy the riches of heaven with Him.

The hard times and pain Christians endure in this life are small and temporary. They cannot even begin to compare with the magnificent glory God will reveal in His people. Keeping your eyes on eternal glory makes present hardships much lighter to bear.

The physical world is waiting with eager anticipation for the day God openly reveals who His children really are. Right now, believers look like ordinary, struggling people whose future honor is hidden. When Christ returns, creation will rejoice as God reveals the glory given to His family.

Creation was plunged into decay and frustration not by its own choice, but because God placed a curse on the earth after human sin. Yet God did not leave the world without hope. The universe was designed to be repaired and restored rather than abandoned to ruin.

The created world will one day be set completely free from the chains of rot, decay, and death. It will share in the wonderful freedom that belongs to God's glorified children. God will renew the physical universe so that it reflects His beauty without any flaw.

The entire creation has been groaning together in deep pain like a mother giving birth. These sufferings are not signs of hopeless death, but the birth pangs of a brand-new world. All of nature waits for the moment of its promised release.

Believers also groan inwardly as they wait for God to complete their adoption by raising their bodies from the grave. Even though they already have the Holy Spirit as a foretaste of heaven, their bodies still face illness, pain, and death. Christians look forward to the day of resurrection when their rescue will be total.

Believers were saved in the posture of hope, looking forward to a finished salvation they cannot yet see. Hope only exists when someone is waiting for something in the future. Once a person already holds a gift in their hands, there is no longer any need to hope for it.

Because believers hope for a glorious future they cannot yet see, they wait for it with quiet patience. Trusting God's promises gives them the staying power to endure hardships without quitting. Real hope produces steady endurance in difficult times.

The Holy Spirit steps in to help believers carry the heavy burden of their weaknesses. Often people are so distressed or confused that they do not know what to ask for in prayer. In those moments, the Spirit Himself intercedes for them with deep feelings and groans that words cannot express.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: The Spirit's groans that cannot be uttered refer to praying in the spiritual gift of tongues.

notes.meaning: God searches human hearts and knows the mind of the Holy Spirit completely. The Spirit always asks for things that match God's good and perfect plan for His holy people. Because the Father and the Spirit are in total agreement, these prayers are always heard.

God actively works through every circumstance in life to bring about good for those who love Him. These are the people He has called to be His own according to His eternal purpose. Even painful losses and difficulties are turned by God into spiritual blessings that prepare His people for eternity.

Long before time began, God lovingly set His eyes on His people and decided their future. He determined that they would be reshaped into the likeness of His Son, Jesus Christ, in character and holiness. This gives Jesus the place of honor as the firstborn brother among a huge family of redeemed children.

differ.view: God's foreknowledge is His sovereign, unconditional choice to set His saving love on particular individuals before creation.
God's foreknowledge means He knew in advance who would freely choose to trust in Christ, and He predestined all such believers to be like His Son.

notes.meaning: God called the people He predestined, declared them righteous by forgiving their sins, and brought them to final glory. This plan of salvation is so certain from God's point of view that their future glorification is spoken of as already accomplished. God Himself faithfully completes the work He starts.

differ.view: This golden chain of salvation is unbreakable, guaranteeing that every person who is effectually called and justified will certainly persevere to final glory.
These steps describe God's general method of leading believers home, but an individual who is justified may still fall away and be lost before glorification.

notes.meaning: Considering all that God has done, believers can be sure that no enemy can ever truly defeat them. If the Almighty God is on our side, no power on earth or in hell can destroy our salvation. Trusting God's friendship drives away fear of any opponent.

God did not hold back His own beloved Son, but gave Him up to die on a cross for all His people. Since He freely gave the greatest treasure in heaven, He will certainly provide every smaller thing needed along the way. Christians never need to doubt that God will provide what is best for them.

No one can bring a charge against God's chosen people that will stand in the court of heaven. God Himself is the supreme Judge, and He has already declared them pardoned and righteous. When the ultimate Judge clears your name, no accusation from an enemy can do any harm.

No one can sentence a believer to hell because Jesus Christ died to pay their penalty. Even more, Christ rose from the dead and now sits in highest honor at God's right hand, where He constantly speaks up for His people as their defender. With the living Savior pleading your case, you are entirely safe.

Nothing can ever tear a believer away from Christ's fierce, protective love. Sickness, emotional distress, persecution, starvation, homelessness, danger, and execution cannot make Him stop loving His people. No matter how bad things get, Christ holds on tightly to those who belong to Him.

Scripture shows that God's people have always faced constant danger and mistreatment simply because they follow the Lord. They are often treated like sheep marked out for slaughter by a cruel world. Suffering for your faith does not mean God has forgotten you; it has been the normal experience of God's servants throughout history.

In the middle of all these harsh trials, believers win an overwhelming victory. This victory does not come from human grit, but through Jesus, who loved them and gave Himself for them. Hardships cannot destroy a believer's faith when Christ is the one giving strength.

Paul states his absolute certainty that nothing in the universe can cut believers off from God. Neither the terror of death, nor the struggles of life, nor good or bad angels, nor evil rulers have that power. Whatever troubles are happening right now, and whatever may happen in the future, are all under God's control.

No extreme heights of success and no deep depths of misery can separate God's people from His care. Nothing in all of created reality has the strength to break the bond of love that God established in Christ Jesus our Lord. Resting in this unbreakable love gives every Christian lasting peace.
